standard.title: Draw conclusions based on analysis
standard.description: draw conclusions based on analysis of information
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3S05): Students drew evidence-based conclusions about community change, environmental features and place connections.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students draw conclusions from analysis of information about risks, resources, exploration, ecosystems and civic issues.

nodes.label: Drawing analytical conclusions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can draw conclusions about historical, geographical and civic topics by analysing sources, with conclusions grounded in evidence rather than opinion.
nodes.minimum_width: Draw at least one conclusion from analysis of at least two sources on a HASS topic.
nodes.typical_width: Describe risks in past times (sea travel, exploration, colonisation); explain how seeking resources connects to trade, exploration, colonisation and environmental change; analyse sources to answer questions about ecosystems, local government services and school rules.
wider: Draw conclusions that connect historical events (e.g. colonisation) to present-day circumstances (e.g. land ownership, environmental change)
Compare conclusions drawn from historical and geographical sources about the same topic and identify where they converge or diverge

response_modes.reason: Year 4 conclusions must integrate multi-source analysis — use structured templates that require evidence from at least two sources before a conclusion can be stated.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Conclusions that connect historical events to present circumstances (colonisation → land ownership) represent the highest-order historical thinking at Year 4 — they transform history from past to relevant.
success_criteria: States at least one conclusion grounded in analysis of sources
Conclusion goes beyond restating facts to explain a relationship or pattern
